easy.def: To do what you are told.
examples: My dog will obey when I say "sit."
We obey the school rules.
The horse obeys the rider.

more.def: To do what a person, rule, or law tells you to do.
examples: Drivers must obey the traffic signs.
Soldiers must obey their orders.
The well-trained dog obeyed every command.

easy.def: A thing you can see and touch.
examples: A ball is a round object.
What is that object in the sky?
Put each object in the box.

more.def: A thing that you can see and touch, but that is not alive.
examples: There was a shiny object at the bottom of the pond.
Sharp objects should be kept away from babies.
A telescope helps you see objects in space.

easy.def: A reason you give for not liking something.
examples: I have no objection.
Her objection was that it was too late.
Does anyone have an objection?

more.def: A statement saying that you do not agree with or like something.
examples: Dad had no objection to our going to the park.
The class raised an objection to the new rule.
Her main objection was that the price was too high.
I have an obligation to feed the dog.
She has an obligation.
It is your obligation.

more.def: A duty or promise that you must keep.
examples: I have an obligation to help my brother.
She kept her obligation to the team.
You have an obligation to tell the truth.
The obnoxious noise bothered me.
An obnoxious kid.
The smell was obnoxious.
The loud, obnoxious noise bothered everyone.
An obnoxious boy kept poking the others.
The smell of the old fish was obnoxious.
The writing was obscure.
An obscure path is in the woods.
The meaning is obscure.

more.def: Not well known, or hard to see or to understand.
examples: The writing on the old stone was too obscure to read.
She loves obscure books that few other people have heard of.
An obscure path led off into the woods.

easy.def: To hide something or make it hard to see.
examples: The clouds obscure the sun.
Fog obscured the road.
A hat obscured his face.

more.def: To make something hard to see or to understand.
examples: Thick clouds obscured the top of the mountain.
A big hat obscured his face from the camera.
Heavy fog obscured the road so drivers had to slow down.
The scientist made an observation.
Observation helps us learn.
My observation was that the plant grew.

more.def: The act of looking at something closely, or what you notice by doing so.
examples: The scientist made an observation about the bird.
Careful observation helps us learn.
My observation was that the plant grew faster in the sun.
We observe the ants as they work.
We observe the moon at night.
The cat observes the bird.

more.def: To watch someone or something closely in order to learn about it.
examples: The class observed how the caterpillar changed over two weeks.
Doctors observed the patient overnight.
If you observe the sky tonight, you may see a comet.
The observer sat very still.
The observer wrote down what she saw.
I am an observer today.

more.def: A person who watches something carefully, often to learn about it.
examples: A careful observer noticed the bird building its nest.
The observers took notes as the experiment began.
An observer at the game counted every point.

easy.def: Thinking about one thing all the time.
examples: He is obsessed with trains.
She is obsessed with her new game.
I am obsessed with dinosaurs.

more.def: Unable to stop thinking about something because you like it so much.
examples: He is obsessed with trains and talks about them all day.
She is obsessed with her new video game.
The kids were obsessed with the new toy.

easy.def: Thinking about one thing all the time.
examples: He has an obsession with trains.
The obsession grew.
Her obsession is soccer.

more.def: A strong, constant interest in something that fills your mind.
examples: An obsession with winning ruined the game for him.
Her obsession with cats made her collect them.
Video games became an obsession.
A log was an obstacle.
The obstacle course is fun.
She overcame the obstacle.

more.def: Something that blocks your way or makes it hard to do something.
examples: A fallen log was an obstacle on the trail.
We ran an obstacle course at camp.
She overcame every obstacle.
A log was an obstruction in the road.
The obstruction was removed.
An obstruction blocked the pipe.

more.def: Something that blocks a path or a passage so that things cannot get through.
examples: A fallen tree was an obstruction on the road, so cars had to go around.
A leaf was an obstruction in the pipe, and the water stopped flowing.
The workers cleared the obstruction from the track.
I obtained a ticket.
She obtained a book.
He obtained the key.

more.def: To get something, often by asking or trying.
examples: I obtained a ticket at the gate.
She obtained a library card.
The club obtained permission to use the gym.
The answer is obvious.
It was obvious she was sad.
An obvious mistake.
The answer was obvious to everyone.
It was obvious that the dog was happy.
The hole in the roof was an obvious problem.

easy.def: In a way that is easy to see.
examples: He was obviously sad.
It was obviously broken.
She was obviously tired.

more.def: In a way that is easy for everyone to see or understand.
examples: She was obviously excited about the trip.
The window was obviously broken.
He obviously loved his dog.
